sentences.text:
This appeal is filed calling in question the judgment and award dated 18.09.2018 in MVC No.684/2015 on the file of the Additional MACT-II and Principal Senior Civil Judge and CMJ,
Bidar, (for short, 'the Tribunal').

The Tribunal, by its impugned judgment and award dated 18.09.2018, has granted a total sum of Rs.30,64,584/- to the respondents - claimants along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum holding that the appellant would be liable to pay compensation.
The Tribunal has also provided for apportionment and deposit.

The Insurer has filed this appeal calling in question quantum of compensation, and the Insurer is aggrieved by the Tribunal computing the loss of dependency taking the monthly income of the deceased Sri Rajkumar at Rs.15,000/- and adding 25% thereof towards future prospects.

2. It is obvious on reading of the grounds urged in the memorandum of appeal that the appellant-Insurer NC: 2023:KHC-K:1360-DB does not dispute that Sri Rajkumar died because of the injuries suffered in the road accident on 19.06.2014 and that the claimants - respondents are his dependents and also that the offending vehicle (Jeep bearing registration No.KA-18/M-2411) was insured with it.
According to the appellant, the Tribunal should not have taken income at Rs.15,000/- per month as the claimant - respondents have not led any evidence to establish the actual income of the deceased.

3. The claimants - respondents have contended that the deceased Rajkumar was ordinarily residing in Mumbai working for his brother Sri Deva Patil @ Dayanand Patil, who was running milk distribution enterprises under the name and style 'M/s. Deva Milk Distributor.
The deceased was visiting the claimants when he met with the fatal accident.

The claimants - respondents contend that the deceased was working for his brother for over 10 years in Mumbai, and as such, he was earning monthly salary of Rs.25,000/- and he was NC: 2023:KHC-K:1360-DB also earning about Rs.5,000/- per month from agricultural operation.
4.

Indeed, the claimants - respondents have not produced any documentary evidence to establish the income of the deceased, but they have produced evidence to show that the deceased's brother Sri Deva Patil @ Dayanand Patil is running enterprises in milk distribution in Mumbai and filing annual returns with the Sale Tax Registration.
Apart from these documents, a Registration Certificate issued in Mumbai Shops and Establishments is produced as Ex.P261.

These documents do support the claimants - respondents' case that the deceased was working in Mumbai and if he was indeed working in Mumbai it would not be an exaggeration to say that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Significantly, Sri Rajkumar is survived by his wife, two minor children and a dependent mother but only Rs.40,000/- is allowed towards loss of consortium.
In all these circumstances, this Court is not persuaded to opine that there is any reason for interference, and as such, the appeal stands dismissed.
The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal for disbursement subject to its order in that regard.

Sd/-
